questions.stem: State the wavelength and frequency changes for blueshift.
questions.modelAnswer: Blueshift shortens the wavelength and raises the frequency as the source approaches.

questions.stem: Explain why redshifted light has a lower frequency.
questions.modelAnswer: Light travels at a fixed speed, so wavelength and frequency trade against each other; a stretched wavelength must come with a reduced frequency.

questions.stem: A star's spectral lines sit at shorter wavelengths than the reference. State the star's motion.
questions.modelAnswer: Shorter wavelengths mean blueshift, so the star is moving towards the observer.

questions.stem: State what redshift provides evidence for.
questions.modelAnswer: Redshift provides evidence that the universe is expanding and supports the Big Bang theory.

questions.stem: State the relationship between a galaxy's distance and its speed away from us.
questions.modelAnswer: The further away the galaxy, the faster it moves away from the Earth.

questions.stem: Explain why redshift supports the idea of an expanding universe.
questions.modelAnswer: The spectral lines of distant galaxies are stretched towards red because the universe's expansion stretches the light waves, showing the galaxies are moving away — and the more distant the galaxy, the greater the shift and the faster the retreat.

questions.stem: Galaxy P shows a small redshift; galaxy Q, further away, shows a large one. Compare their speeds.
questions.modelAnswer: Galaxy Q recedes faster: greater distance goes with greater redshift and therefore a greater speed away from Earth.
